fit: review of cholinergic and visual mechanisms in Parkinson disease
assessment: This review synthesizes visual hallucination studies involving cholinergic dysfunction, Lewy pathology, visual attention and distributed brain circuits. It describes reports in medication-naive patients and an earlier levodopa challenge with no elicited episodes. The underlying observations are medication and mechanism leads, with no dried fig comparison.

fit: autopsy tissue and diagnostic group comparison
assessment: Autopsy groups with Alzheimer disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, mixed disease, Parkinson disease dementia and controls were compared on regional tau, amyloid and synuclein burden. The design measures neuropathology by diagnostic group; dietary fig consumption and episode timing are absent.

fit: actigraphy and clinical features across Lewy body diagnoses
assessment: Eleven participants with dementia with Lewy bodies, 12 with Parkinson disease and 11 age-matched controls completed clinical and rest-activity measurements. The study compares motor activity and circadian patterns across clinical groups. Core symptom information is clinical context and was not tied to dried fig or meal timing.

fit: secondary clinical sample and PPMI visual status with fMRI
assessment: PPMI classified 25 Parkinson participants with a broad hallucination or psychosis item and compared them with 56 Parkinson participants without symptoms and 24 controls. The separate ICICLE-PD sample used a dedicated visual interview and a severity score combining frequency, duration and type. Resting connectivity and subsequent clinical measures were compared without dried fig or other food-timed episode counts.

fit: visual episodes after neurosurgical conditions with vision loss
assessment: Two institutional cases and 17 patients from 13 papers document visual phenomena in a neurosurgical Charles Bonnet context. Some episodes were restricted to visual field loss. These are different underlying conditions and there is no oral food comparison.

fit: Parkinson visual hallucination status and paracingulate MRI
assessment: The comparison uses MRI in 32 Parkinson participants with visual hallucinations and 33 without them. The regression explicitly uses presence versus absence. The anatomic findings address group status without an ingredient exposure or a counted change in frequency.

fit: visual symptoms as prognostic evidence in longitudinal cohorts
assessment: The systematic review includes people without dementia at enrollment and studies subsequent diagnoses of dementia with Lewy bodies, Parkinson disease dementia or broader Lewy body dementia. It evaluates prior visual symptoms as possible predictors, without a dried fig comparison or post-meal episode outcome.

fit: neuroimaging and Parkinson visual hallucination group status
assessment: Groups of people with Parkinson disease with and without hallucinations were compared on imaging measures of networks involving the amygdala and nucleus basalis of Meynert. The association is based on clinical group status. The food exposure, temporal attribution and episode frequency required for the frozen claim were absent.

fit: cross-sectional prevalence of minor and formed Parkinson hallucinations
assessment: The study included 372 people with Parkinson disease. It recorded 114 with one or more minor phenomena and 55 with visual hallucinations, with overlap. These counts describe people and clinical phenotypes, rather than the number of episodes after food consumption.

fit: retrospective Capgras delusion and co-occurring visual reports
assessment: The retrospective study extracts Capgras misidentification and other clinical features from Lewy body disease records, with matched imaging subsets. Co-reported visual hallucinations and the delusional misidentification phenotype are distinct observations. There is no fruit exposure or post-intake episode rate.

fit: clinical minor hallucination status and visual-to-semantic performance
assessment: The clinical sample has 93 Parkinson outpatients, 55 without hallucinations and 38 with minor phenomena. The group comparison uses visual-to-semantic assessments. Those task measures and a history of minor phenomena do not provide repeated visual event counts after a meal.

fit: mouse behavior used as a proxy for visual hallucinations
assessment: The experiments distinguish locomotion, staring, eye-tracking and responses in a pharmacological mouse model. Observable behaviors are proxies for an inferred state and carry no patient account of spontaneous visual episodes. The original does not administer dried fig.

fit: resting EEG and visual symptom status in dementia with Lewy bodies
assessment: Resting high-density EEG compares 33 early dementia with Lewy bodies participants with 21 controls. Visual hallucination and REM sleep behavior status are examined separately in relation to alpha-band connectivity. There is no monitored fig exposure or change in the number of visual episodes.

fit: task-evoked visual processing with Parkinson visual symptoms
assessment: The clinical sample from NCT03661125 comprised 18 people with Parkinson disease without hallucinations and 20 meeting Parkinson psychosis criteria. A dedicated interview characterizes visual phenomena. The experiment compares visual mismatch EEG and model-based connectivity, with no food intervention or food-timed clinical episode rate.

fit: observational Parkinson infusion outcomes and adverse reports
assessment: Ten observational studies of continuous subcutaneous levodopa strategies contributed to the review. Motor effects and reported neuropsychiatric adverse events concern medication exposure and heterogeneous follow-up, without a dietary ingredient comparison.

fit: genetic Parkinson case with subcutaneous and oral drug changes
assessment: A case of PINK1-related Parkinson disease describes timed plasma drug measurements and neuropsychiatric observations while infusion, oral levodopa and a COMT inhibitor were adjusted. Several medication changes preclude a single-exposure comparison. Dried fig was not an exposure.

fit: clinical observational adverse events after Parkinson infusion
assessment: The 77-person advanced Parkinson chart review records seven new hallucination cases during subcutaneous levodopa prodrug infusion, usually distressing and at night. The table separately counts other psychiatric events and reports median time to first hallucination of 14 days. This is onset during a drug exposure with treatment adjustments, with no dried fig intake or counts of repeated episodes.

fit: PPMI early hallucination-related status and brainstem MRI
assessment: The study uses PPMI structural scans and item 1.2 during screening or early follow-up as a proxy for hallucination-related status. The item does not separate all visual subtypes and modalities. MRI-derived volume and presence or absence of the broad proxy do not provide food-timed episode frequency.

fit: fig leaf-derived cell-culture extract applied to skin
assessment: Forty healthy exam-period students ages 20–27 used active cream or vehicle in two groups of 20 in a reported double-blind comparison. The article reports lower transepidermal water loss at recovery with active cream and separate cultured skin-cell measurements. The exposure is topical leaf-derived cell-culture extract, with no whole fruit ingestion or visual episode outcome.

fit: common fig fruit used as an assay reagent
assessment: The study uses fig fruit to make a fluorescent probe and applies it to aged cheese, cured meat, sausage, pickled olives and canned fish. The authors report a calibration range of 5–400 ng/mL and a quantitation limit of 1.68 ng/mL. Those values describe the method. The abstract gives no fig tyramine concentration or clinical outcome.

fit: injected derivative and rat striatal receptor expression
assessment: The rat experiment measured striatal receptor transcript levels after systemic N-methyl-norsalsolinol exposure. Serotonin 5-HT2A and delta-opioid transcripts rose; mu-opioid expression fell. The clinical hallucinosis link is the authors' interpretation. The abstract provides no measurement of food-derived salsolinol, fig ingestion or observed visual episodes.
